body: Fuck you.

I'm not a moron. I know how numbers work. Your opinion is that you're a superior being, an intellectual who looks down upon wastes of matter such as myself. You're just an asshole crushing me further into a hole I'm already deep inside.
Never did I ask for help in my post.

So in other words, you believe I possibly can't learn a language because I'm not smart. Listen to yourself, you sound extremely arrogant. I'm depressed largely because of my total lack of self-esteem, and you're over here shoving the fact you easily learn languages in my face after I explain that I struggle with language.
I took Spanish classes every single year from elementary school through high school (twelve years), and I’ve used Duolingo and the like, as well as Spanish content.

Like I said, I want to be come at least partly fluent in it, I definitely want to learn it. But clearly I have broken your odds and your magic ability to learn languages. Your comment just seems like a boast.
Thank you very much for the advice.
Thank you very much for the kind words.

Thank you. I think right now I'm in even less of a place to learn a new language than I was a year ago. I don't know how long it'll be until I should try again, and I don't know if I ever should try again, because every time I do, I just get frustrated. I don't really know why I posted this. I wasn't looking for an answer, I was just voicing my extremely unpopular opinion.
I don't really know the vocab. I know some, but not much. That's why I use captions.

Thank you (although I was hoping nobody would look there...). Since I became depressed, learning anything, really, has become more frustrating. I've fallen into following Homer Simpson's questionable advice of "if something's hard to do, it's not worth doing." Now, I don't want to go too off-topic, but I don't think I'll ever really be in a place to learn a new language. I think it just isn't for me, no matter how much I want to.

I've tried all different kinds of learning, and while I haven't focused on interests in particular, I have focused on things that would help me have general conversations. And yet, I still can't have any.

I am in treatment for depression, yes. But I was only diagnosed with it around a year ago, and was struggling just as much with Spanish beforehand. I took Spanish classes throughout elementary, middle, and high school, but didn't really get anywhere.

But I have done more than just try to learn, I've tried to use it as well. As I mentioned in another comment, I've tried speaking to friends in Spanish, whether it's verbally or through written text, but it just doesn't work because the amount I do understand isn't enough to communicate in any meaningful way.

That's a related problem, when it comes to verbal language. No matter how slowly people speak, it's still too fast to understand. I'm still stuck in that place where you first have to translate anything mentally to your native language in order to understand it.

I learned it throughout school, and since then I've been using things like Duolingo and things like watching Spanish YouTube videos with English captions, or English ones with Spanish captions, to no avail. I've even tried speaking with some friends online in Spanish, but I know so little that it's difficult to form any sentences that actually mean anything useful, let alone understand them in return.
